cards.text: Paul the apostle just told the elders of the church in Ephesus they'd never see his face again, and they all wept (Acts 20:25, 37-38). Now Paul and his travel crew tear themselves away and sail to Cos, then Rhodes, then Patara. And in city after city, the Holy Spirit has warned him that chains and afflictions are waiting (Acts 20:23).

cards.question: At Patara, Paul's crew finds a ship crossing over to a new region. Where's it headed?

cards.text: They spot Cyprus, pass south of it and land at Tyre in Syria. And friend, that ship isn't stopping because Paul asked nicely.

cards.question: So why does the ship stop at Tyre?

cards.text: They look up the disciples in Tyre and stay SEVEN DAYS. That's not a layover, friend, that's moving in.

cards.question: Through the Spirit, the disciples in Tyre keep telling Paul not to go up to ___.
After all those warnings in Tyre, Paul calls off the trip and stays there.

cards.text: When the week's up, the whole church walks them out of the city, wives and children too. That's not a goodbye, friend. That's a PARADE.

cards.question: Down on the beach outside Tyre, what does everyone do before Paul's crew leaves?

answers.text: Read a letter from Ephesus together

cards.text: Goodbyes said, Paul's crew boards the ship and the folks from Tyre head home. The voyage ends at Ptolemais, where they greet the brothers.

cards.question: Paul's crew stays with the brothers in Ptolemais for ___.

cards.text: Leaving the next day, they go on to Caesarea and stay at the home of Philip the evangelist, one of the Seven chosen to serve the church back in Acts 6:5. Tyre got a week, Ptolemais got one day, and now Philip's guest room is about to get BUSY.

cards.question: Philip has four unmarried daughters who prophesy.

cards.text: Several days in, a prophet named Agabus comes down from Judea. Watch this one, friend.
Agabus walks over, takes a belt and ties up his own feet and hands with it. No hello, no small talk, friend, just a grown man tying himself up in the middle of the visit.

cards.question: Agabus ties up his own hands and feet with a belt. Whose belt is it?
Agabus says the Holy Spirit says the Jews of Jerusalem will bind the owner of this belt and hand him over to the ___.

cards.text: Paul's crew and the people of Caesarea hear it, and they ALL plead with Paul not to go up to Jerusalem. Me? I'd have wrapped my mustache around his ankle and held on.

cards.question: Paul answers the people pleading with him. For the name of the Lord Jesus, what does he say he's ready for in Jerusalem?

answers.text: To be bound and even to die
To argue his case in court
To preach and then slip away

cards.question: Paul tells the people pleading with him that their weeping is breaking his heart.
Paul won't be talked out of going, so his friends quiet down. What do they say?

cards.text: After these days, they pack up and go on to Jerusalem. Two cities warned him, friend, and Paul still packs like he's got FRONT-ROW TICKETS.

cards.question: Who goes along with Paul's crew on the way to Jerusalem?

cards.text: Those disciples take them to stay at the home of Mnason the Cypriot, an early disciple. Warned in Tyre, warned in Caesarea, and Paul keeps right on going, friend.

findings.problem: The opening card never says where Paul is heading. Jerusalem is the center of this passage, and Acts 20:22 states it. Without it, the baker has nothing to reason from on card 6 ("not to go up to ___"), so that card becomes a guess. Name Jerusalem as Paul's destination on this card, with its reference.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: How long the crew stayed at Ptolemais (one day) doesn't move the passage forward, and the baker isn't helped by knowing it. The baker can't reason it out either. Tell it on the story card and give this choice card to a moment that matters.

rule.text: Ask about the moments that move the passage forward and the details the baker needs to understand it.

findings.problem: The joke doesn't land. "Tyre got a week, Ptolemais got one day" sets up a pattern about how long they stay, but "Philip's guest room is about to get BUSY" doesn't finish that pattern. A baker would have to stop and work out what "busy" means.

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: The right answer, "The Lord's will be done," is the only one that sounds like Scripture. "Then go on without us" and "We tried our very best" sound modern and casual, so the right answer is easy to spot.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: "Paul still packs like he's got FRONT-ROW TICKETS" gives Paul an eager, excited feeling as if it were fact. The text gives no feeling here, and just before this Paul says the weeping is breaking his heart and that he is ready to be bound and to die (Acts 21:13).

rule.text: Feelings: He can guess at a feeling, marked as his own ("I think," "I bet"). Never as fact.

findings.problem: The second sentence, "Warned in Tyre, warned in Caesarea, and Paul keeps right on going," repeats the beat from card 11 ("Two cities warned him... Paul still packs"). It is a recap, not a step forward through the passage.
